parts.headline: RFQs pay in 30 days. RFPs pay in a year.
paragraphs: First federal buy I won was an RFQ. About $42,000 for service parts. Six emails over four days, a one-page price sheet with a short technical narrative, a PO in my inbox the next Tuesday. The money hit the bank thirty-one days after invoice.

Every founder I talk to is chasing the $5M RFP. They should be chasing forty RFQs first. Faster cash, fewer competitors, real past performance built one CLIN at a time. That past performance is what unlocks the bigger work later.

This playbook is the version I wish I'd had on that first one. What an RFQ actually is, where it lives (eBuy vs SAM.gov), how to price it, and the seven-box checklist that keeps a quote from getting tossed for the wrong reason.
Run a quote a week. Build the muscle. The cash flow alone is worth it.

parts.partLabel: PART ONE · WHAT AN RFQ ACTUALLY IS
parts.headline: An RFQ is not a small RFP. The rules are different.
paragraphs: Request for Quote lives under FAR Part 13 — Simplified Acquisitions. The threshold is $250,000 for FY2026, the evaluation is usually price plus delivery plus past performance, and the response window is days, not months.
Get the category wrong and you'll over-engineer a 60-page proposal for a buy that wanted a one-page price sheet. The next pages cover what an RFQ actually requires and how GSA Schedule quotes work.

parts.markdown:
RFQ FUNDAMENTALS
# The fastest path to federal revenue. The Request for Quote is the federal government's streamlined buying mechanism for purchases under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. Three numbers that matter:
ThresholdWindowCompetition
$250K
SAT ceiling, FY2026		 10 days
Typical quote window		 3 quotes
Minimum for most SAT buys
## RFQ vs RFP — Know the difference.
ElementRFQRFP
ThresholdUnder SAT ($250K)Any amount; common >$250K
FormalityInformal quote / orderFormal proposal with volumes
FAR ReferencePart 13 (Simplified Acq.)Part 15 (Negotiation)
EvaluationPrice + delivery + past perfTechnical + mgmt + price
Contract TypePO or BPA callFFP, T&M, Cost-Plus
Response TimeDays to 2 weeks30-90 days typical
Protest RightsLimitedFull GAO rights
FIELD TIP
If you see 'RFQ' on a buy over $250K, read again. It's almost certainly a GSA Schedule order under FAR 8.4 — different rules, same word.

GSA SCHEDULE QUOTES · FAR 8.405-2
# eBuy is where Schedule quotes live. If the RFQ is against a GSA Schedule vehicle (MAS, OASIS, STARS III), the rules shift. Same word, different game.
RuleWhat it meansWhat to do
Hold the Schedule Your firm must hold the relevant GSA Schedule AND the SIN must cover the scope. Check SIN coverage first. Adding one takes 60-90 days.
Three-quote min Agencies must compare 3 Schedule holders before awarding (FAR 8.405-2). Watch eBuy daily. Respond fast — be one of the three.
Quote via eBuy ebuy.gsa.gov is the portal. Email and phone quotes don't count. Register primary + backup notification email.
Price ceiling Your price must be at or below your GSA-negotiated catalog rate. Discount off catalog when the buy is competitive.
Orders >$25K Agency may require a brief technical approach, key personnel, refs. Read the RFQ. Submit exactly what they ask for.
WHY THIS MATTERS

GSA Schedule quotes are where most small primes get their first repeatable federal revenue. Set up the alerts, respond inside the window, price under catalog. Six months of that and you have a real federal book.

parts.headline: Seven moves separate the winning quote from the rest.
paragraphs: Most disqualifications on RFQs aren't about price. They're about a missing CLIN, a name that doesn't match SAM.gov, or a delivery date the contracting officer doesn't believe.
The next two pages cover the seven practices that win quotes — and the seven-box checklist to run before you hit send.

parts.markdown:
QUOTE RESPONSE BEST PRACTICES
# Seven moves that win quotes.
#MoveWhy it works
1Read the RFQ completelyThe CO writes the disqualifications into the RFQ. Read them first.
2Confirm POP deliveryLate delivery is recorded in CPARS and shows up in every future eval.
3Research fpds.govIf the last three buys went for $42-48 per unit, don't quote $61.
4Price competitively, not recklesslySAT buys go low — but sub-market pricing flags you as a risk too.
5Include a brief tech narrativeOne page is enough. Gives the CO something to point at on award.
6Aggressive delivery only if realFast delivery wins ties. Missed delivery is a negative past-perf event.
7Confirm payment termsVerify your SAM banking is current — net 30 EFT goes to that record.
FIELD TIP
Build a quote template before you need it. One-page Word doc — company info, CLIN table, delivery box, T&Cs, signature. When the 10-day window lands, you fill in numbers, not format.

QUOTE RESPONSE CHECKLIST
# Seven boxes. Run them before every submit. A missed box is the easiest disqualification in federal. The CO doesn't owe you a chance to fix it. Tick each before you hit send. - [ ] Quote covers all required line items (CLINs) exactly as specified - [ ] Delivery date confirmed with the team actually doing the work — call the warehouse or PM, don't guess - [ ] Pricing includes all costs: labor, materials, shipping, installation. Burdened, not raw - [ ] Company info matches SAM.gov registration exactly (legal name, address, UEI) - [ ] POC contact info included (name, title, email, phone) - [ ] Quote signed by an authorized representative — not the intern who built the doc - [ ] Submitted via the correct method: email to the listed CO, eBuy portal, or fax for the legacy agencies
WHY THIS MATTERS

We've seen quotes lose on price by $4,000 that should have been disqualified for a SAM.gov name mismatch. The CO caught the mismatch on the winner and re-awarded. Don't be the firm that wins on price and loses on paperwork.
